notes: terra: The psalmist calls his days a declining shadow and himself withered grass, joining the waning day to a life running out.

notes: terra: Harvest and summer have ended and “we are not saved,” making a closing season the figure of missed rescue.

text.KJV: The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.

notes: terra: The disappearing day and stretched evening shadows turn late light into an urgent warning.

text.SBLGNT: ὥστε ⸂αὐτοὺς ἡμᾶς⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν ⸀ἐγκαυχᾶσθαι ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὑμῶν καὶ πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς διωγμοῖς ὑμῶν καὶ ταῖς θλίψεσιν αἷς ἀνέχεσθε,

notes: terra: Patience is needed to receive the promise after doing God’s will, joining endurance to faithful action.

text.KJV: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.
text.SBLGNT: ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν·

notes: terra: Patience is to complete its work, making endurance productive rather than merely passive.

text.KJV: But let patience have [her] perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
text.SBLGNT: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω, ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι, ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι.

notes: terra: The wicked must drain the dregs of the Lord’s cup, using wrung-out liquid as an image of judgment.

text.KJV: For in the hand of the LORD [there is] a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring [them] out, [and] drink [them].
text.WLC: כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים שֹׁפֵ֑ט זֶ֥ה יַ֝שְׁפִּ֗יל וְזֶ֣ה יָרִֽים׃

notes: terra: Those who plant pleasant vineyards will not drink their wine, matching the loss of fruit one expected to enjoy.

text.KJV: Forasmuch therefore as your treading [is] upon the poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.

notes: terra: Waters surround the speaker even to the soul, matching the inverted image in which water itself becomes choking danger.

text.KJV: The waters compassed me about, [even] to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.

notes: terra: Wishing needy people well without giving necessities exposes the emptiness of withheld help.

text.KJV: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be [ye] warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what [doth it] profit?
text.SBLGNT: εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, ⸀τί ὄφελος;

notes: terra: The whirlwind scatters people like chaff and a rolling thing, matching the storm’s power to lift and disperse what stood on the ground.

text.KJV: The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but [God] shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.

notes: terra: Rain, floods, and winds strike a house until it falls, matching a storm that suddenly destroys accumulated security.

text.KJV: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.
text.SBLGNT: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.

notes: terra: Christ’s self-giving offering is a sweet-smelling savour, paralleling fragrance as the trace of a beneficent act.

text.KJV: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.
